name: Sandmere Athletic

location.about: A coal town of about 90,000 on the cliffs twelve miles up the coast from Whitcombe: the pits went down under the sea, and the last one closed in 1993. Now a seaside town with long beaches, a lighthouse and a fierce pride in its club.

colours.story: Rose pink and black - the colours of the Sandmere Lodge's banner, carried by the miners at the Durham gala every July. The club was formed by the lodge in 1881 and took its colours.

home.shirt: rose pink with black collar and black cuffs

third.shirt: white with a pink and black hoop

rivals.why: the shipbuilding city twelve miles down the coast - pits against yards, since 1881; Whitcombe's money has never felt bigger
the 1992 title race, won by Sandmere on goal difference

history.title: The lodge team
history.text: Formed by the Sandmere miners' lodge in 1881. Second Division champions in 1894, up and down for forty years (runners-up in 1901, 1910 and 1926); the Founders' Cup in 1921; Second Division champions again in 1938.

history.title: The pitmen's title
history.text: Champions in 1952 - the club's first title, with eleven pitmen's sons in the side - the Founders' Cup in 1959, and in 1970 the title and the Charter Cup, and the Founders' Cup final lost: one game from the Treble.

history.title: The pits close
history.text: Up and down: promoted in 1979, the Charter Cup in 1981 and 1982, second in 1982 and 1986, relegated and back as champions in 1988 - and champions again in 1992, the year before the last pit closed. The Charter Cup in 1995.

history.title: The yo-yo
history.text: Relegated, and back as runners-up in 1997; the Europa Trophy in 2003, the club's only European trophy (after losing the 1992 final); down, Second Division champions in 2008, down, champions again in 2010; down again in the 2010s, and up as runners-up in 2018.

history.title: Rose pink again
history.text: Second in the league in 2024 - the best season for thirty years - while Whitcombe's new money won it two years running down the coast.

honours_note: League seasons are given by the year they ended (1952 = 1951-52).

legends.name: Jack Shotton
legends.note: A hewer at the Sandmere pit, captain of the 1952 champions.

legends.name: Ronnie Pyle
legends.note: Promotion, the 1992 title and the 1995 Charter Cup. The Pyle Stand is named after him.

legends.name: Kenny Bewick
legends.note: Scored twice in the 2003 Europa Trophy final.

records.attendance: 68,512 v Whitcombe City, League, 1950 (The Lodge, before seating)

badge.about: The pithead winding wheel and the lighthouse on the cliff; the lodge's pink and black. Motto 'Ex Profundis' - from the depths.
badge.design: A rose-pink shield with a black border. In the centre a black pithead winding wheel on its frame, and beside it a white lighthouse on a black cliff. Three wavy black lines for the sea at the bottom. 'SANDMERE ATHLETIC' arched above the shield in black capitals, and a black ribbon beneath reading 'EX PROFUNDIS' in pink, with '1881' on the ribbon's ends.

ground.name: The Lodge

stands.name: Pyle Stand
stands.features: the main stand: tunnel, dugouts, a row of boxes; the Lodge banner hangs in the reception

stands.name: Pit End
stands.features: the home end - one steep single tier in pink seats, a restored winding wheel on its own outside

stands.name: Sea Stand
stands.features: two tiers with the North Sea right behind - the wind comes straight off it

ground.surroundings: the cliff top: the North Sea and the beach right behind the east stand, a lighthouse on the headland, the restored winding wheel of the old pit, rows of miners' terraced houses
ground.atmosphere: windswept, loud and proud - pink scarves and the Lodge banner on derby day

for_the_engine.notes: a windswept ground on the cliffs
